claims.text: The untreated target alloy has excellent caloric performance under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The untreated target alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
A tailored post-synthesis annealing treatment can induce fine coherent nanoscale precipitates in the target alloy.
The desired precipitates may be an ordered L12-type intermetallic phase.
The precipitates will be distributed uniformly throughout the target-alloy matrix.
Fine L12 precipitates impede dislocation motion through Orowan bowing and bypass, thereby increasing strength.
The nanoscale precipitates will act as crack arresters and impede crack propagation.
Precipitation strengthening will enhance yield strength and overall integrity in the target alloy.
The precipitates can strengthen the target alloy while maintaining the phase-transformation mechanism responsible for its caloric effect.
Annealing may improve compressive and tensile strength by tens to more than 100 MPa relative to the untreated target alloy.
Annealed samples will exhibit less cracking under load than untreated samples.
Annealed samples can retain more than 90% of the untreated alloy's caloric performance.
The intervention should work best in the field and temperature regime where the caloric transition is active.
Formation of coarse or secondary brittle phases could degrade the caloric effect.
Post-synthesis annealing should be conducted under an inert or controlled atmosphere to avoid unwanted oxidation or secondary-phase formation.
The optimal annealing temperature and duration for the target alloy have not been established.
The hypothesis is falsified if annealing fails to produce a statistically significant mechanical-integrity improvement while retaining at least approximately 90% of the baseline caloric response.
